title: Runtime hint propagation API sketch
content:
Goal / motivation:
- Provide a minimal, low-friction API surface for clients (SDK + edge proxies) to attach lightweight runtime hints to requests so the serving runtime can make smarter batching / prefetch / fallback decisions without expanding the public API surface or changing model semantics.
- Hints should be advisory only (do not change model output), small, and safe for pass-through across trust boundaries.

Design principles / constraints:
- Compact: <= 4KB total header/payload for hints (target ~256B typical).
- Backwards-compatible: absence of hints = default behavior.
- Best-effort semantics: hints can be dropped by intermediate proxies if size/latency constraints demand.
- Privacy-safe: no PII or raw user content allowed in hints. Only labels, numeric scores, and stable non-sensitive tokens.
- Versioned: allow v0, v1 in header for graceful evolution.

High-level propagation model:
- SDK -> Edge (optional) -> Ingress Gateway -> Router -> Serving Runtime
- Hints travel as a single JSON blob in an HTTP header X-Runtime-Hints (base64 or compact-encoded).
- Gateways MAY drop or truncate hint blob when under load. Router and runtime should log when a hint is missing for observability.

Header format (text sketch):
- X-Runtime-Hints: v1;eyJkaXMiOiJfIiwiYXQiOnsicHJpb3JpdHkiOjUsInByZWZldGNoIjoiY29kZS10aW1lIn19
  - prefix 'v1;' indicates encoding version, rest is base64-encoded compact JSON.

Compact JSON schema (v1) - fields are all optional and small:
{
  "dis": "string - dispatch token, opaque to runtime (<= 32 chars)",
  "at": {"priority":"int (1..10)", "urgency":"float (0..1)"},
  "prefetch": {"class":"small-string","budget_ms":"int"},
  "cost_hint": {"max_tokens":"int","prefer_quantized":"bool"},
  "privacy": {"sensitivity": "none|low|medium|high"},
  "ttl_ms": "int - soft time-to-live for prefetched KV / warm cache",
  "tags": ["short-tag-strings"],
  "routing": {"region_pref":"string","tier_override":"string"}
}

Notes on fields and semantics:
- dis (dispatch token): small developer-chosen token to correlate across systems; opaque to runtime but useful for telemetry. e.g., "signup-flow-1a"
- at.priority: integer used for lightweight scheduling / admission control in edge/ingress. Lower=more important. (1 highest priority).
- prefetch.class: categorical hint that indicates which prefix/context the request will likely need. Examples: "user-profile-l2", "recent-docs", "code-completion-typed". Runtimes can map classes to prewarm strategies.
- prefetch.budget_ms: soft budget for prefetch cost (e.g., how long to spend warming caches).
- cost_hint.max_tokens: upper bound on expected output size (for batching cost planning).
- cost_hint.prefer_quantized: boolean allowing runtime to prefer quantized model variants when cost-sensitive.
- privacy.sensitivity: prevents some cache/prefetch behaviors; e.g., "high" should avoid persisting context to multi-tenant caches.
- ttl_ms: how long prefetched KV/prefix warm state can remain hot.
- tags: freeform short strings for SRE routing rules / canary selectors.
- routing: region or tier preferences (best-effort).

Encoding / size considerations:
- Use short field names in v1 (dis, at, pf, ch, pv, t). The sketch uses readable names for clarity; real encoding should minimize bytes.
- Base64 + header may bloat. Alternatively support compact-safe header encoding (URL-safe base64 or 7-bit hex). Consider allowing a separate side-channel for larger hint blobs (X-Runtime-Hints-Ref: refid) with small header pointing to ephemeral metadata in ingress state store.

API / SDK ergonomics:
- Provide simple SDK helper: RuntimeHints({dispatch, priority=5, prefetchClass=null, budgetMs=null, maxTokens=null, preferQuantized=false, sensitivity='none', tags=[]}) -> header string.
- Server-side SDK (ingress) should expose whether hints were preserved or dropped (for telemetry) via response header X-Runtime-Hints-Applied: true|false and a reason code (truncated, dropped-by-ingress, invalid).

Runtime-level behavior examples:
- Example 1: low-latency interactive assistant
  Client hint: {dis:'assistant-intent', at:{priority:1}, prefetch:{class:'assistant-shortctx', budget_ms:15}, cost_hint:{max_tokens:80}, privacy:{sensitivity:'low'}}
  Runtime action: ensure KV cache is warmed for 'assistant-shortctx', schedule request into low-latency lane, prefer smaller batch sizes, avoid quantized fallback.

- Example 2: background summarization job triggered by user action
  Client hint: {dis:'background-summary', at:{priority:7}, prefetch:{class:'summary-prewarm', budget_ms:200}, cost_hint:{max_tokens:512, prefer_quantized:true}, privacy:{sensitivity:'medium'}, ttl_ms:600000}
  Runtime action: allow larger batching, pick quantized model variant, prewarm KV with TTL, do not persist beyond ttl and obey privacy constraints.

Safety & privacy rules (non-negotiable):
- Hints MUST NOT contain raw user content, PII, or full prompt fragments. If SDK detects that a user string is used as a label, it must hash/sanitize it before embedding in hint.
- High-sensitivity hints should prevent cross-tenant caching and disallow routing to non-compliant tiers.

Observability / metrics:
- Emit metrics: hints_received_total, hints_dropped_total (by reason), hint_field_usage_{fieldname}, prefetch_hit_rate_by_class, hint_applied_latency_delta_{bucket}.
- Log sampled request traces that include decoded hint blob for debugging (redact tags and dispatch tokens in high-sensitivity cases).

Rollout / compatibility strategy:
- Start with v1 in SDK behind feature flag. Server logs whether hint header seen. Run A/B experiments comparing latency/cost for requests with and without hints using small opt-in apps.
- Expose admin UI in Console showing most-used prefetch classes and mapping suggestions (Optimize product integration).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to authenticate / integrity-protect hints from clients in hosted scenarios? Should we allow signed hints from private deployments only?
- Do we want a binary compact TLV encoding instead of tiny JSON to shave bytes? Pros/cons: binary is smaller but harder to introspect in logs.
- Side-channel ref store: cost/availability implications, lifecycle for refids, abuse vectors.
- Should 'priority' be absolute or a soft percentile compared to tenant baseline?
- Mapping of prefetch.class to actual KV keys—should mapping live in runtime config (Console-managed) or be embedded in app config?

Follow-ups / action items:
- Diego: prototype SDK serializer + header parser (JS + Go) (INF-3421)
- Lin: add hint_received_total and hints_dropped_total metrics to ingress (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987)
- Maya: small A/B design doc for canary users and suggested prefetch class set for SDK v0.1 (confluence:Runtime-hint-patterns)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep field names short for encoding (pf vs prefetch). Use semantic version in header so we can evolve.
- Consider a safe default whitelist of prefetch classes shipped in SDK to reduce operator surprises.
- Evaluate cost impact: prefetching increases GPU warm state but can reduce tail latency; need model-specific cost calculator.

References / similar ideas:
- Ingress-admission priority headers (internal SRE notes)
- Client-side prefetch hints in mobile networking (HTTP/2 early hints concept)
- Existing internal 'warm-classes' mapping in Optimize team config

End of sketch.
